aws_code_build_project: `aws_code_build_project` defines a real, fully managed build, its source, build environment, and buildspec, that AWS CodeBuild compiles, tests, and packages into deployable artifacts, run standalone or as a stage in an `aws_code_pipeline_pipeline`.
aws_code_build_report_group: `aws_code_build_report_group` collects real test and code-coverage reports generated by an `aws_code_build_project`'s own builds into one place, so results across many build runs can be reviewed and trended together instead of inspected one build log at a time.
aws_code_commit_repository: `aws_code_commit_repository` creates a private, fully managed Git repository in AWS CodeCommit, encrypted at rest and in transit, supporting standard Git commands and tools. AWS CodeCommit stopped onboarding new customers on July 25, 2024; existing customers with a repository can continue creating additional ones and using the service as normal.
aws_code_connections_connection: `aws_code_connections_connection` links AWS to an external source provider, GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, once authorized, so a real `aws_code_pipeline_pipeline` or other AWS service can pull code without re-authenticating per use. AWS CodeConnections is the March 2024 rename of AWS CodeStar Connections; the older `aws_code_star_connections_connection` resource type continues to work.
aws_code_deploy_application: `aws_code_deploy_application` is CodeDeploy's own top-level container name, ensuring the correct combination of revision, `aws_code_deploy_deployment_config`, and `aws_code_deploy_deployment_group` gets referenced together each time a real deployment runs.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_config: `aws_code_deploy_deployment_config` defines the real rollout pace an `aws_code_deploy_deployment_group` deploys with, one instance at a time, half at a time, or all at once, among CodeDeploy's predefined configs, or a custom one.
aws_code_deploy_deployment_group: `aws_code_deploy_deployment_group` is the real, specific set of EC2 instances, an Auto Scaling group, or an ECS service and load balancer, that an `aws_code_deploy_application`'s revisions actually get deployed to, along with when to reroute traffic and when to retire the old version.
aws_code_guru_profiler_profiling_group: `aws_code_guru_profiler_profiling_group` is the real unit CodeGuru Profiler aggregates and analyzes application performance data under, one or more applications' profiling agents all reporting into the same group so performance issues can be identified across them together rather than per application.
aws_code_guru_reviewer_repository_associ: `aws_code_guru_reviewer_repository_association` connects a real source repository to Amazon CodeGuru Reviewer for automated code review. As of November 7, 2025, CodeGuru Reviewer is in maintenance mode and closed to new repository associations; existing associations continue working, with Amazon Q Developer's own code review capabilities positioned as the real successor.
aws_code_pipeline_custom_action_type: `aws_code_pipeline_custom_action_type` defines a caller's own real action an `aws_code_pipeline_pipeline` stage can invoke, beyond CodePipeline's built-in source, build, test, and deploy actions, for integrating a tool AWS doesn't provide a native action for.
aws_code_pipeline_pipeline: `aws_code_pipeline_pipeline` models the real, automated stages, source, build, test, deploy, that a code change moves through on its way to release, the core, top-level resource every other CodePipeline resource attaches to.
aws_code_pipeline_webhook: `aws_code_pipeline_webhook` triggers an `aws_code_pipeline_pipeline` execution the moment a real external event happens, a GitHub push, for instance, rather than the pipeline polling its source on an interval to notice a change.
aws_code_star_connections_connection: `aws_code_star_connections_connection` is the pre-rename CloudFormation resource type for what's now `aws_code_connections_connection`, AWS CodeStar Connections having been renamed AWS CodeConnections in March 2024. Existing connections and this resource type continue to work; the old APIs stopped being available after April 2025.
aws_code_star_connections_repository_lin: `aws_code_star_connections_repository_link` ties a real, specific repository to an `aws_code_star_connections_connection`, a persistent reference CodePipeline's V2 pipeline types and other AWS services use for source actions rather than resolving the repository from the connection alone each time.
aws_code_star_git_hub_repository: `aws_code_star_git_hub_repository` creates a GitHub repository as part of the original AWS CodeStar service's own project setup. AWS discontinued creating and viewing CodeStar projects on July 31, 2024; resources CodeStar already created, including this repository, its source repos, pipelines, and builds, continue functioning unaffected.
aws_code_star_notifications_notification: `aws_code_star_notifications_notification_rule` sends real notifications, to Slack via AWS Chatbot, to SNS, to email, when a specific event happens in a CodeCommit, CodeBuild, CodeDeploy, or CodePipeline resource. Despite the shared name, this service was unaffected by CodeStar's own 2024 discontinuation and remains active.
aws_cognito_identity_pool: `aws_cognito_identity_pool` issues real, temporary AWS credentials, via AWS STS, to authenticated or guest users, accepting claims from an `aws_cognito_user_pool`, a SAML 2.0 provider, or a social identity provider, independent of whether a user pool is used alongside it.
aws_cognito_identity_pool_principal_tag: `aws_cognito_identity_pool_principal_tag` maps an `aws_cognito_identity_pool`'s real claims from one specific identity provider into IAM principal tags on a user's temporary AWS STS session, enabling attribute-based access control policies keyed on those tags.
aws_cognito_identity_pool_role_attachmen: `aws_cognito_identity_pool_role_attachment` maps real IAM roles to an `aws_cognito_identity_pool`, by default role, by rules against a user's claims, or by their `aws_cognito_user_pool_group` membership, the actual configuration that determines which role a user gets credentials for.
aws_cognito_log_delivery_configuration: `aws_cognito_log_delivery_configuration` routes an `aws_cognito_user_pool`'s own real audit and activity logs, sign-in events, user notifications, by event source and log level, to a specific CloudWatch Logs log group, rather than that activity going unrecorded outside CloudTrail's own API-call logging.
aws_cognito_managed_login_branding: `aws_cognito_managed_login_branding` applies real visual branding, logo, colors, layout, to an `aws_cognito_user_pool`'s managed login pages through a no-code visual editor or a large set of programmatic style options, rather than every sign-in page looking like Cognito's own unbranded default.
aws_cognito_terms: `aws_cognito_terms` configures real terms of use and privacy policy document links for an `aws_cognito_user_pool_client`, shown on managed login's sign-up page in the language matching the user's own locale, with a defined fallback when no localized document exists.
aws_cognito_user_pool: `aws_cognito_user_pool` is a real, standalone user directory and OIDC identity provider, sign-up, sign-in, and federation with third-party IdPs, that issues JWTs directly to an app, independent of whether an `aws_cognito_identity_pool` is ever used alongside it.
aws_cognito_user_pool_client: `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` registers a real, specific application, a web app, a mobile app, a backend service, against an `aws_cognito_user_pool`, with its own allowed OAuth flows, callback URLs, and token settings, the actual identity a caller authenticates as when it talks to the user pool.
aws_cognito_user_pool_domain: `aws_cognito_user_pool_domain` hosts an `aws_cognito_user_pool`'s real managed login pages, either a Cognito-provided prefix domain or a custom domain, the authorization and web server that federated and local sign-in actually happens through.
aws_cognito_user_pool_group: `aws_cognito_user_pool_group` creates a real, logical grouping of users inside an `aws_cognito_user_pool`, listed in the ID and access tokens Cognito issues, and usable to map a user to a specific IAM role when a token is passed to an `aws_cognito_identity_pool`.
aws_cognito_user_pool_identity_provider: `aws_cognito_user_pool_identity_provider` federates an `aws_cognito_user_pool` with a real external identity source, Google, Facebook, SAML 2.0, or another OIDC provider, mapping that provider's claims into the standardized JWT the user pool issues to an app.
aws_cognito_user_pool_regional_configura: `aws_cognito_user_pool_regional_configuration_attachment` configures an `aws_cognito_user_pool`'s real, Region-specific settings, including its email delivery configuration, SES sender address, configuration set, distinct from the user pool's own core identity and authentication settings.
aws_cognito_user_pool_replica: `aws_cognito_user_pool_replica` creates a real, secondary copy of an `aws_cognito_user_pool` in another AWS Region for multi-Region failover, supporting a growing subset of authentication and session operations locally depending on whether the replica is active or inactive.
aws_cognito_user_pool_resource_server: `aws_cognito_user_pool_resource_server` defines a real API an `aws_cognito_user_pool` can issue OAuth access tokens scoped to, the mechanism behind machine-to-machine authorization and fine-grained API access control in Cognito rather than a single, undifferentiated access token.
aws_cognito_user_pool_risk_configuration: `aws_cognito_user_pool_risk_configuration_attachment` configures real adaptive authentication for an `aws_cognito_user_pool`, scoring each sign-in for risk based on IP address, device, and behavioral factors, and requiring extra MFA or blocking the attempt outright at higher risk levels.
aws_cognito_user_pool_uicustomization_at: `aws_cognito_user_pool_uicustomization_attachment` applies CSS and logo customization to an `aws_cognito_user_pool`'s legacy Hosted UI (classic) sign-in pages, the older customization mechanism that `aws_cognito_managed_login_branding` supersedes for user pools on managed login.
aws_cognito_user_pool_user: `aws_cognito_user_pool_user` is a real, individual user record created directly inside an `aws_cognito_user_pool`, administrator-created rather than self-registered, with its own attributes and initial credential state.
aws_cognito_user_pool_user_to_group_atta: `aws_cognito_user_pool_user_to_group_attachment` is the real, actual membership grant linking an `aws_cognito_user_pool_user` to an `aws_cognito_user_pool_group`. Neither existing on its own makes a user a group member, this attachment does.
aws_comprehend_document_classifier: `aws_comprehend_document_classifier` trains a real, custom model on caller-labeled documents, plain text, PDF, Word, or images, to categorize new documents into the caller's own classes, single-label or multi-label, run synchronously in real time or as a batch job against a whole document set.
aws_ecr_repository:
`aws_ecr_repository` creates a real, private ECR repository for storing
container images, with real, configurable scanning and mutability
settings.
aws_iam_policy:
`aws_iam_policy` creates a standalone, reusable IAM policy, a real JSON
document describing what's allowed. It grants nothing on its own,
attach it to a role or user with `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment` to
actually apply it.
aws_iam_role:
An IAM role grants a set of permissions to whatever's allowed to assume
it, an EC2 instance, a Lambda function, another AWS account. `aws_iam_role`
creates the role and its trust policy, real permissions are attached
separately, via `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment`.
aws_iam_role_policy_attachment:
`aws_iam_role_policy_attachment` is the actual grant, it attaches an
existing, standalone policy to an existing role. Neither the role nor
the policy alone grants anything, this attachment is what connects
them.
aws_s3_bucket:
`aws_s3_bucket` creates the bucket itself. Versioning, encryption,
public-access blocking, and lifecycle rules are each their own separate
resource, attached to this bucket by reference, real Terraform provider
behavior since v4.
aws_sqs_queue:
Amazon SQS is a fully managed message queue. `aws_sqs_queue` creates
and configures one, standard or FIFO, with a real, typed binding in
every SDK language.
aws_vpc:
`aws_vpc` creates a real, isolated virtual network, the real
foundation every other real networked resource, subnets, security
groups, route tables, gets placed inside.
